cover_text: Mahatma Gandhi1 once said, “The world provides enough for the needs of nations, but not for the wants of nations.” This was also the epoch where the roots of in-country unrest started in the Swadeshi cause of developing a cooperative market between India and Britain. The Sankranti and the Ganesh Chaturthi festivals were initiated by Gandhi, with the mango and glutamian residues from the ground lands being used as the poison which was the root of discontentment to the capitalist steady economy. The tradition of celebrating the festivals in the nationalistic manner grew after Gandhi’s death and due to its purity of origin – independent and free – was pitted with each other and created a sour company of individuals (Bhadra 1114). The proprieties and norms present in these celebrations fell short of what Gandhi had since they also deposed society’s traditional practices as deficient, and following the fight with Himlett the Indians found this new approach reluctantly and used the symbol of the woman to represent desirableities and power in a new jhoom platform. The new actions were guided bewax and initiation of violent protests on over 18 communal camps in Gujarat.
